name: underlivers-agents
description: Underlivers Agents: a fork of Pixel Agents (MIT) where your Claude Code agents work in a pixel office, with name tags, an all-women team, a boss and speech bubbles

commands.title: Underlivers Agents: Export Layout as Default

pixel-agents.autoShowPanel.description: Automatically open and focus the Pixel Agents panel when VS Code starts.

pixel-agents.autoSpawnAgent.description: Automatically spawn a Claude Code agent when VS Code starts, if no agents are currently running.

pixel-agents.showNameLabels.description: Show a name tag above every character: the agent's name in bold, its role below. A spawn described as "<Name> · <domain> · <item>" shows the name and "domain · item"; any other description is shown cut to fit. The lead session wears a ★ boss marker.

enumDescriptions: Only the bundled characters that are women (char 1, 3, 5 and 6-10). Characters from external asset directories are always included.
pixel-agents.characterSet.description: Which characters new agents are drawn from. Applies to agents created after the change.

pixel-agents.characterByName.description: Fixed character (char_N index) per agent name, so a named sub-agent or teammate always has the same face. Names not listed get a stable hash of their name into the allowed set.

enumDescriptions: Speech bubbles from the speech banks.
Speech bubbles plus the line's voice file from ~/.pixel-agents/speech/<name>/ when there is one.
pixel-agents.speech.description: Whether named characters talk (lines come from the speech banks: dist/speech/*.json, overridden by ~/.pixel-agents/speech/*.json).

pixel-agents.speechFillerMinutes.description: Minutes of silence after which an idle named character says a filler or a word of encouragement. 0 = never.

pixel-agents.speechSpicy.description: Adult register: idle fillers and answers to the boss's visits sometimes come from the banks' "coquine" lines (crude, explicit, fictional adults). Off: those lines are never sent to the office.

pixel-agents.bossName.description: Name on the lead session's tag ("★ <name>", role "boss") and the speaker of its lines (speech bank with the same speaker name).

pixel-agents.bossCharacter.description: Character (char_N index) every lead session wears, whatever pixel-agents.characterSet says. 0 = the man in the suit. -1 = drawn like any agent.

pixel-agents.bossArea.description: Area label of the lead's own office: the lead takes a seat there first, and named sub-agents (employees) get desks outside it. Empty = upstream seating (sub-agents stand next to their lead).

pixel-agents.bossVisitMinutes.description: While active, the lead walks over to one of its named sub-agents at least this often (it also visits when it hands one a task or messages her). 0 = only on those events.

pixel-agents.bossChat.description: Standalone office: show the chat panel with the boss (messages go to ~/.pixel-agents/boss/inbox.jsonl, answers come from outbox.jsonl).

scripts.compile: npm run asyncapi:generate && npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js && npm run build:webview
scripts.package: npm run asyncapi:generate && npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js --production && npm run build:webview
scripts.lint: eslint adapters/vscode server core && cd webview-ui && eslint .
scripts.lint:fix: eslint adapters/vscode server core --fix && cd webview-ui && eslint . --fix
scripts.test: npm run test:webview && npm run test:server && npm run test:package-contract
